                                        II. JURISDICTION

3. This Court has jurisdiction over this matter pursuant to 28 U.S.C. § 1332, as there is diversity

of citizenship between Plaintiff, a citizen of Ghana, and Defendant, a Delaware corporation with

its principal place of business in California, and the amount in controversy exceeds $75,000.


                                            III. VENUE

4. Venue is appropriate under 28 U.S.C. § 1391 because the Defendant's principal place of

business is in Mountain View, Santa Clara County, California, and the events giving rise to this

claim occurred within this judicial district.


                             IV. INTRADISTRICT ASSIGNMENT

5. Jurisdiction and venue are further proper under Clause 16.8 of Google's Developer

Distribution Agreement, which mandates the resolution of disputes in the federal courts located

in Santa Clara County, California.


                                   V. STATEMENT OF FACTS

6. The plaintiff, Dynasto Afedo, is a citizen of the country Ghana, in Africa (West Africa).


7. The defendant, Google LLC, is incorporated under the laws of the State of Delaware and has

its principal place of business in the State of California.


8. Plaintiff Dynasto Afedo, an independent game developer from Ghana, files this complaint

against Google LLC ("Google") for its systemic failures in account verification processes,

breaches of the Developer Distribution Agreement ("DDA"), discriminatory practices, and unjust

termination of Plaintiff's second developer account.

9. Plaintiff seeks relief for significant financial harm, reputational damage, and systemic barriers

imposed by Google's actions, which disproportionately affect underrepresented developers,

including Plaintiff.


10. The plaintiff alleges damages amounting to $20,000,000 (Twenty Million US Dollars),

including compensatory, consequential, and punitive damages, as well as injunctive relief to

remedy the harm caused by Google's actions.


                                    A. Developer Background


11. Plaintiff, Dynasto Afedo, is a resident of Ghana and an independent software developer with

over 10 years of experience in the industry. On August 29, 2014, the plaintiff made a one-time

payment of $25 to Google, which granted him access to a Google Play Developer Account,

subject to Google's written agreement known as the Google Developer Distribution

Agreement. This account enabled the plaintiff to publish apps and games on the Google Play

Store (Account ID: 7668574642906869929 / thedynasto@gmail.com).


12. Throughout his career, the plaintiff has successfully developed and published a variety of

mobile applications, including one of Africa's most successful racing games, RWC Racing. This

game has garnered significant attention and success in the gaming market.


13. Plaintiff is an accomplished game developer who has achieved over 64,000 downloads on the

Google Play Store and 120,000 downloads across all platforms, including iOS.


14. Plaintiff's track record on the Google Play Store demonstrates compliance with Google's

policies and significant contributions to the app development ecosystem, providing valuable

content and user engagement globally.

        Case 5:25-cv-01884-NC           Document 1        Filed 02/21/25     Page 4 of 27




                                 B. Account Verification Failures


15. Since 2023, Plaintiff has encountered significant issues with Google's account verification

process, which requires developers to verify their accounts using phone numbers and other

methods.


16. Despite multiple compliance efforts using valid Ghanaian phone numbers, Plaintiff was

unable to complete the verification process, resulting in the inability to update or republish apps.


17. Verification was only successful when Plaintiff used a VPN to simulate a U.S.-based IP

address, highlighting systemic barriers.


18. The Plaintiff's second developer account was unjustly terminated despite full compliance

with Google's verification requirements.


                             C. Discrimination and Systemic Failures


19. The verification system disproportionately impacted the Plaintiff, creating significant

obstacles to accessing the global app market.


20. Google's verification issues perpetuate inequities in the app development ecosystem, unfairly

restricting Plaintiff's access to equal opportunities.

21. Google Developer Distribution Agreement Clause 2.2: Google will not permit the

distribution of Your Products through Google Play, and You may not accept the Agreement

unless You are verified as a Developer in good standing.


22. Google Developer Distribution Agreement Clause 4.3: You are responsible for maintaining

the confidentiality of any developer credentials that Google may issue to You or that You may

choose Yourself, and You are solely responsible for all Products that are developed under Your

developer credentials. Google may limit the number of Developer Accounts issued to You or to

the company or organization You work for.


Violated by: Google LLC


23. Clause 2.2 Explained: Developers must be verified and in good standing for their products

to be distributed on Google Play.

24. Clause 4.3 Explained: Developers are responsible for maintaining valid credentials, but

Google must facilitate the process and ensure reasonable access to accounts.

25. Clause 2.2 and 4.3 Violation: Google failed to ensure verification of the Developer Account,

depriving Plaintiff of the ability to update and manage apps and generate revenue despite

complying with Google's policies.

undertaking or handling the support and maintenance of Your Products and any complaints about

Your Products. You agree to supply and maintain valid and accurate contact information that will

be displayed in each of Your Products' detail page and made available to users for customer

support and legal purposes. For Your paid Products or in-app transactions, You agree to respond

to customer support inquiries within 3 business days, and within 24 hours to any support or

Product concerns stated to be urgent by Google.


Violated by: Google LLC

meaningful recourse for support to users regarding his products.

hindering potential opportunities for future growth.

                                 VII. DEMAND FOR RELIEF


WHEREFORE, Plaintiff respectfully requests that this Court grant the following relief:


36. Award Plaintiff damages in the amount of $20,000,000 (Twenty Million US Dollars),

including:


  a. Compensatory damages for direct financial losses such as lost revenue and development

costs.


  b. Consequential damages for projected future earnings losses and missed business

opportunities, as well as reputational harm affecting Plaintiff's partnerships, user engagement,

and credibility.


  c. Punitive damages to penalize Defendant for systemic failures, breaches of contract, and

discrimination, and to deter similar misconduct in the future.


37. Order Defendant to fulfill the terms of the contract.


38. Issue an order compelling Defendant to reinstate Plaintiff's second developer account.


39. Require Defendant to implement equitable verification processes that address and eliminate

systemic barriers for underrepresented developers.


40. Award additional damages due to Defendant's refusal to mediate, arbitrate, or address these

issues in good faith, leading to unnecessary litigation and procedural escalation.

1. Background of the Case:


Since 2023,1 have encountered significant issues with Google's new verification process. Despite

multiple attempts to verify my account using different phone numbers, I have been unable to

effectively. This culminated in notices that my account would be terminated, and my second

IP address, revealing systemic barriers faced by developers in underrepresented regions like mine.

reputation as a game developer.

I am currently located in Accra, Greater Accra, Ghana, and appearing in person would cause

significant hardship due to several factors.

       foreign exchange rates exhaust my resources, making it financially difficult for me to

       allocate the necessary funds to hire an attorney while also providing for my family.

       before the Court has put a pause on my source of livelihood until the case is resolved.

I have substantial evidence to support the claims raised in this case, including an admission from

the defendant regarding the issues at hand.


This case involves complex matters requiring expertise in high-tech litigation, including:

The complexity of these issues necessitates a deep understanding of technology, software

agreements, and platform operations. Without legal representation, I would face significant

challenges in navigating this case's technical and legal intricacies and effectively presenting my

claims.



4. Efforts to Obtain Counsel:



I have made extensive efforts to secure legal representation for this case but have been

unsuccessful due to financial constraints. My efforts include:


   • Contacting legal clinics, law firms, and the state bar for assistance;

   • Utilizing referral materials and services to find pro bono or low-cost counsel;

For the reasons outlined above, I respectfully request that the Court appoint pro bono counsel to
